name: Pharaoh
overview: Pharaoh is the male ruler of Egypt during the time of Israel's Exodus, as noted in Exodus 3:10. His exact tribal affiliation and personal details are not recorded in Scripture. He is a central figure in the narrative of Israel's deliverance from Egyptian bondage.
namesAndTitles: The title 'Pharaoh' identifies him as the supreme ruler of Egypt, a designation not given by God but used to signify his authority. He is also referred to as the 'King of Egypt,' which plainly means the king over the land of Egypt, underscoring his political and national leadership role as recorded in Exodus 3:19.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Pharaoh beyond his role as the ruler during Israel's Exodus. No specific relatives or familial connections are mentioned in the biblical text provided.
scriptureSignificance: Pharaoh is significant in the biblical narrative as the primary antagonist during Israel's deliverance from slavery. His resistance to God's command to release the Israelites sets the stage for God's demonstration of power and faithfulness. Through Pharaoh's hardened heart, God's sovereignty and the fulfillment of His promises to His people are vividly displayed.
